(a) we have developed a method for the fast clearing of large human tumour resectate samples, (b) we have developed an imaging protocol for the 3D visualization of the cleared tumours, and (c) we have demonstrated that the cleared tumour resectats and the corresponding H&E/IHC sections show morphological similarities.
we have developed a novel technique to 3D visualize tumours, which allows pathologists to study the 3D architecture of tumour-host tissue interfaces.
we have established a novel method to visualize 3D histopathological structures in human tumours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new imaging technology that enables pathologists to analyse the 3D architecture of human malignancies.
the development of an ultrafast clearing and imaging technique for 3D histopathological diagnostics of human tumours.
the development and evaluation of a novel 3D imaging technique that allows the visualization of the tumour-host interface in a large number of histological structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presented approach is a valuable addition to the histopathologist's toolbox, which allows the 3D analysis of tumour resectate samples in a non-invasive and non-destructive way.
this technology is a novel, fast, non-invasive, and non-destructive technique to visualize and analyze the morphology of large human tumour resectations in 3D.
the combination of ultrafast clearing and light sheet imaging enables a new dimension of histology, which allows for a more comprehensive analysis of tumour-host tissue interfaces.

we have developed a new technology to visualize tumour tissue in 3D.
we have developed a novel technique that combines the advantages of 3D imaging with the advantages of H&E staining.
we present a novel approach to 3D imaging of human tumours, which is based on a combination of fast clearing and ultrahigh-speed microscopy.

the combination of ultrafast clearing, light-sheet microscopy and computational image processing can be used for the 3D analysis of human tumours.
we provide the first demonstration of 3D imaging of large tumour samples with a resolution that is sufficient for diagnostic purposes.
